name: registry-endpoint
definition: Subject operates the service at the given URL (registry, verifier, MCP server or A2A agent).
title: Registry endpoint
description: Binds a service endpoint to an Agent ID through an ordinary attestation, so a client can find where an identity runs a registry, verifier, MCP server or A2A agent and check that the statement is logged. Attestations only: agent traffic is never logged (spec section 16 point 5).

kind is one of registry, verifier, mcp, a2a, or an extension name beginning with x-. A signed A2A agent card is carried by hashing the card JSON into the attestation evidence field and pointing evidence-uri at the card.

A log validates url (an https URL of at most 2048 characters with a host, no credentials and no whitespace) and kind at admission (schema_invalid); the core verifier does not check it. It is the seventh claim type of the core list of Draft 05, which with the seven robotics claim types makes 14.
issued-by: The endpoint operator (usually the subject itself, or its domain owner)
subject: Agent ID the endpoint belongs to
attestation-schema:
attestation = {
  subject: agent-id,
  issuer: agent-id,                      ; MUST equal the envelope signer
  claim: uri,
  data: { * tstr => any },
  ? evidence: bstr .size 32,
  ? evidence-uri: uri,
  id: bstr .size 16,
}
agent-id = bstr .size 32
uri = tstr
data-checked-by: Logs at admission (schema_invalid); the core verifier does not check it.
lifetime: 30 to 180 days by default, 400 days at most
